additional_source_checks.supports: Python Doc initialization stores the identifier without name validation.
Python conversion sets the native primary key and converts fields; under stated valid-string/schema assumptions it does not reject TAB before native Insert.
set_pk copies the string without identifier validation.
WriteResults is a vector of Status.

evidence_review.coverage_limit: Curated evidence is reference support, not a mandatory literal citation list. Small forwarding/type-definition spans inspected additionally establish the API path without requiring a solver to quote every wrapper.

unit_review.reason: Valid UTF-8 below the collection byte limit; space, slash, CJK letters and emoji are not in the forbidden-codepoint set. This does not assert that the whole schema with an invalid field succeeds, nor filesystem safety.
Field validation uses the separate ASCII letter/digit/underscore/hyphen rule and rejects bytes >=0x80; 标题 fails.
The specified ID is valid UTF-8, nonempty, short enough, and contains no rejected codepoint.

The limit is 1024 bytes. U+6C49 汉 takes three UTF-8 bytes; 341 copies have 1023 bytes and pass, 342 have 1026 and fail. These are linked calculations of the one explicitly asked byte-limit rule, not additional unasked requirements.
TAB is expressly forbidden and invalid identifier validation returns INVALID_ARGUMENT.

The initial validation loop returns on the second invalid document before the write loop begins; none of the three is inserted. It need not validate the third after detecting the second, and a correct answer must not be required to assert that it does.

An unexpected overall Result is unwrapped and INVALID_ARGUMENT maps to py::value_error; Python returns no per-item list. Pure Python conversion and native set_pk do not change this under the supplied valid-string/schema assumptions.

All identifiers pass prevalidation. The write loop records Status for each item and returns a value vector. Python unwraps the successful overall Result and returns [OK, ALREADY_EXISTS, OK]; it does not call the overall error mapper on each element.

Fresh first and third items reach successful insertion; the second per-item failure is appended without breaking the write loop. Returned statuses and stored-state effects are distinct observations, so C4.2 and C5.1 are not duplicate points.

The duplicate lookup returns before operator/WAL/internal insertion, preserving old payload under the valid-state/no-other-errors assumptions. The distinction from UPSERT is correct and explicitly requested by asking whether data is overwritten.

assumption_review.verdict: Sufficient for the requested two batch return/state conclusions.
assumption_review.tab_batch: All IDs are new, fields/vectors are compatible, valid Python strings exclude encoding/conversion failures, and no other errors occur. Native validation stops at TAB before any write. No transaction rollback needs to be assumed.
assumption_review.duplicate_batch: The existing seed-id is explicitly live; the first/last identifiers are framed as fresh and the only exceptional condition is the stated duplicate. No concurrent operation, switch, state or I/O error can interrupt the per-item loop. The collection-level ID map makes the duplicate check valid independent of whether seed-id originally resides in the current writing segment.
assumption_review.state_scope: Inserted/unchanged refers to normal collection state after return. The question does not ask for crash durability, fresh-process reopen or a transaction guarantee; none is required by the rubric.
assumption_review.identifier_probe_scope: Probe 1 explicitly restricts itself to identifier validation. Thus it does not imply that a slash-bearing collection name is a filesystem path, or that a schema containing 标题 succeeds overall.
